text: Your medicines are very important
in heart failure.
Your doctor may give you different medicines
to help manage ongoing symptoms.
Heart failure medicines help your heart in many ways.
Some act to lower blood pressure
and improve the pumping function of the heart muscle.
Others work by reducing stress on the heart
or managing extra fluid in your body.
Always remember to take your medicines every day
and follow the instructions from your doctor.
Your doctor may change your dose of medicines over time,
even if you are feeling well.
Keep an updated list of your medicines for you
and your healthcare team to refer to.
Don't stop taking your medicines without speaking
with your doctor or pharmacist.
Ensure you have enough medicine if you are going away
and keep a reminder to fill your prescription
before your medicines run out.
Your medicines can help you live longer
and stay out of hospital.
They will also help you feel better
and have more energy to enjoy life.
And to learn more about managing heart failure,
watch the other videos in this series.
